pages.text: Excessive humility is   a shadow aspect of Dalet. If it is used as a way to receive  praise and to be emotionally taken care of, it will produce disappointment and possibly despair. At times, it can infect relationship with a passive-  aggressive stance that is emotionally  devastating and spiritually false. If this  humility is an illusion that substitutes for accepting help from Hashem, it can be experienced as cruelty and judgment from those in close proximity.  Doorways are sacred. Another shadow aspect of Dalet is acting as if all  doorways to resolve internal wars are closed. Behaving as a victim in  relationships and in the material world creates the belief you are alone and  cannot receive from the divine.  Staying paralyzed in doorways, not making choices, or hiding your “poverty” from the world is another shadow aspect of Dalet. Staying put when it is clear  you need to take action is a sign of fear taking hold.  Right  Actions  for Dalet:  .  Look  at the “doors”  in  your life you have refused to enter. Open  one  at a time  and move through knowing Hashem is moving with you. Notice how that  feels.  Share that experience with a trusted friend.  Talk with a person  you have assumed is  closed to you.  Begin by being like  Dalet. Be a door the  person can move  through. On the  other  side  of that door,  create the  experience  of acceptance  and true  humility. You know  how to  do  it.  Identify and resolve an internal war. Look at and  examine all the possibilities  of each  side. Define the  important  issues.  Choose the possibility  that parallels  your  highest motivations and gives you an experience  of  harmony.  Let  all  the  other  possibilities go free.  Share  the important  lessons  learned.  22

The story  is  told that when Perl,  the wife of a  well known  Rabbi would bake Challot, the special braided bread for Shabbat, she  would  pray,  “Master of the  Universe, I beg of you, when  my  husband says  the blessing over the  bread, he has the  same Holy  intention that lam now  putting into  its preparation.“  HEI  Meaning:   Window, and  the word  “the”  Focus: Movement of thoughts into  action  -  Connections  between  thought, mind, and  action  Number: 5  Calendar  Connection:   Nisan —- March/April  When you choose Hei, it means  you  are  ready  to  explore  your inner,   feminine  nature.  This is  the  gap or  space  that occurs  between  your  thoughts and  your  actions.  This is  true whether  you are a man or a woman.  This gap  is existential  and  when you  allow  existential experiences into your  life,  it means  you  are strong  23

enough to delve into matters of deep personal meaning. This is a necessary precursor for  you to do a “right action.”  What is your experience of the quiet space, the gap, in-between your thinking and  your actions? Take a moment and feel it now.  Hei is a perfectly balanced letter and since our society is a predominately  masculine culture, your choice of the letter Hei is very important. It means you are ready for more balance in your life.  Allowing the feminine principle into your life is crucial for the balance our society is yearning for. The Kabbalah teaches that Hashem gave women an  additional measure of spiritual understanding than He gave to men. Now that you  have chosen Hei, this understanding is available to you. Everyone’s nature includes universality, sensitivity, limitlessness, nurturing, and conservation of life.  Which feminine aspect of your nature is most important to you now? The first  answer that arises no matter what you may think is the one to explore.  As  well as being perfectly balanced,  Hei is  also a broken letter.   You could be  experiencing a broken  relationship, a broken heart, or breaking  away from a career  ora   job that no longer suits you. By choosing Hei, you have heard the whisper of the letter and need the nurturing, feminine, aspect of Hashem. It is time to become  balanced in your life by being close to Hei. The gap between thought  and action  is real.  Although  accessing  that gap is  valuable to your  inner life, it can be  uncomfortable.  The Kabbalah  teaches that  Hashem put this gap in place  so you could  experience  this dissonance, the  choice  between  the  real and the ideal, between thought and  action.  As  you  move forward  spiritually and emotionally, Hei provides you with the  sensitivity to  see your  imperfections,  challenges,  and  brokenness, while embracing  them  all with  Hei’s  harmony. By choosing to experience this gap between  your  thought  and  action,  you  give yourself  this opportunity,  The Kabbalah  teaches  that  when  we  are  active in  this  process of  divine no-thingness,  this gap, we become  true  partners  with Hashem.  The  number for  Hei  is  five.  Consequently, there are five  steps  between each  thought  and  the action taken. They are:  having  the idea  feeling the space  planning the execution  bridging  to the  higher  self  PHONE

5.   acting from the highest good  The Kabbalah also teaches that the end of the action was the first in thought.  This is a Kabbalistic Koan similar to the question, “what is  the sound of one  hand  clapping?”  Do you know what is  meant by the end of the action was the first in  thought? Trace  one of your past actions back to its original thought.  Do you  hear your present thoughts waiting to be brought  into  action?  Do you know  which  of the five-steps  you are comfortable with and which ones give  you the most trouble and stress?  When you share your thoughts with others,  you are  revealing  yourself.  Although this intimacy can feel uncomfortable at first,  when  you get  used to it, it  brings  you exquisite  joy. When  you give yourself to another, you  are giving the  ultimate gift. The ultimate gift is  you. It takes the willingness to experience  intimacy,  (in-to-me-see)  which may feel uncomfortable  at  first.  Shadow Aspect of Hei © When  you utter harsh words to another  instead of  first listening to your  thoughts, you  are demonstrating a shadow aspect  of Hei. Rather than think through what you need  to say, you  ignore the gap  and  do not  take  ownership  of  your  words and  the meaning behind them. This can be devastating  to  all  involved;  words cannot be recalled  after  they  are  spoken. Spoken words are  like feathers  that come  out of a pillow; it is  impossible to gather  them back  once they are let loose.  * When we think that  what we  have to  say  is  most important, we are directly in  the  shadow of Hei. In that  moment we are so self-focused  our idea becomes  all  that  matters. That behavior  psychically  eliminates the  other  person from  our  thoughts,  and  our partnership  with Hashem  disappears.  * When  we engage only one-step  of  the five-stage  process,  and  ignore  the other  four,   we eliminate  our  capability  to live in  that conscious  gap provided by Hashem. We are then unable  to express our authentic  self. We  behave like  robots and shadows  of our  true  self. We live as if on a treadmill,  repeating  our patterns  over  and  over  again.  * It  is  easy to  be  stuck  in  brokenness,  whether  from a relationship,  the  end of a  career,   or a  loss. It can be  dramatic,  possibly  even  familiar  and  self-fulfilling,  25

but ultimately crippling. This shadow aspect of Hei calls to us like the legends  of the sirens that call out to the sailors when they are lonely and desperate.  Is brokenness an illusion or is it real?  Right Actions for Hei:  *   Choose the feelings that come from right action. Remember that many of your thoughts are old patterns and thoughts think. Choose to do what bring you into the creative, feminine principle of Hei. They are the nurturing,  compassionate, forgiving, inspired actions. When other negative, reactive  thoughts appear, notice them, and move on. At one time, they were there to  protect you. No   longer receiving your attention, they will disappear over  time.  *   Write down the actions and experiences you choose to identify with at this time and focus on them each day. Notice what happens to your mood and  perspective.  ¢   When you feel fear in any form, such as anger, resentment or worry,  remember,   your actions are always a choice. Put yourself in that gap between  thought and action. Choose an action that allows the fear to lose its power by  sharing yourself, remembering a positive moment, and knowing that Hashem  is never far away.  *   Before you take action, move into the gap and experience the silence. The  gap is the experience of the Divine. Be aware of the highest good in your  action.  26

Rabbi Meir of   Premishlan used to go to a Mikvah, a sacred,  ritual bath ina   river on a steep hill outside the city. He would make this  trek even on icy, winter days. Once some skeptical   young men tried to  follow the old rabbi up the slippery hill, but they slipped and were so badly injured they needed medical treatment. After the   young men were healed, one of them, somewhat   humbled by  the experience,  dared to ask the venerable  sage  how he could  climb day after  day without   falling.  Rabbi  Meir  replied  in a straightforward  manner: ‘If a person is  connected  above,  he does not   fall down below!’  VAV  Meaning:   Hook, ‘and’ (a conjunction)  27

Focus:   Connection or Link - represents completion.  Number: 6  Calendar Connection: yar: the second month of the Kabbalah year.  (April-May)  By choosing Vav, it means you are ready to connect to all the different aspects of yourself. Right now, you have the fortitude to let go of the power your  past mistakes have over you, and transform your regrets into compassion.  Vav is the sixth letter of the Hebrew Alef-Bet and represents the sixth day of  creation, the day right before Hashem rested. This is the day Hashem completed the creation of the universe. By choosing Vav, you are personally ready to take another  step toward completion, which may include correcting actions from your past, making new choices in the present, and/or creating new visions for the future. It is time to take a clear look at yourself and take charge of your cycle of mistakes,  judgment, and regret.  As you meditate on the shape of the Vav, you can see that it is facing forward to the future while staying grounded in the present. Look at the letter now.  Remember, Hebrew letters read from right to left.  As you meditate on the Vav, what do you think it means to face the future while  staying grounded?  What future vision arose for you from this meditation? What action do you need to take to ground this vision?  There are  some interesting  aspects  to Vav, as you  understand that  the Biblical  Hebrew meaning means Hook and Connection.  ¢   Asa   prefix to a noun, Vav means “and,” so it clearly connects what came  before to what follows.  ¢ Asa prefix to a verb, it changes the  tense of the  verb  from  past to future  or  from future to past giving it transformative powers.  * Vav has the ability to move  backward  or  forward  in  time with  great  power to  help heal the past and envision the future.  The  energy of Vav connects and  brings opposites together. For  example,  past  and future, negative and positive, fear  and joy. When  you remember that  Hashem  created the  universe  from these  Hebrew letters, you  begin  to  understand that  Vav  has the power to support you in “teshuvah,” meaning repentance and  28

transformation. You do “teshuvah” by turning away from fear and negativity, by  facing forward to personal purpose and meaning, to “tikkun,” repair of the world.  How is this important to you now?  The Kabbalah teaches when Hashem created the universe he sent a single ray of light to our world. When this light entered our world, it was so immense and  radiant, there was   a shattering, and the light scattered. You can get a glimpse of  what this might have looked like when walking in the woods and seeing rays of light  filtering through the trees.  The Kabbalah continues by saying Hashem then entered into a partnership with us to repair this shattering. Our commitment in this partnership is to bring all  the sparks or particles of light back to Hashem so together we can create a righteous planet. We can use our free will to help heal that brokenness in the behavior we  choose from moment to moment. Because of this partnership, we sometimes feel our true home is beyond where we stand. We have all heard people speak of wanting to go home  to  Hashem  when  they are ill. By choosing Vav, you have found  the  courage to stay.  When  you bring light and consciousness to your past actions,  you can forgive  yourself and repair the world. By transforming  that  darkness from your past, you  can change your future.  Think of some incident from your past. Just for a moment,  see it as  healed. What  changes need to occur to make this real? This takes  courage. When you  do this with  positive  intention,  you have  decided to whisper the  ineffable name of Hashem  into  the tapestry of your life.  The Shadow Aspect of Vav:  * Many  people  at  this  time in  our  history tend to  be stuck in  the  “light.” They do  not want the  experience  of  just  what is. Instead, they  judge it or  see it as  negative,  or  project  it on others in  the  form of  judgment, racism,  sexism,  etc.  They do not want to  associate  with  this  aspect  of  life.  However,   Vav depends  on what is to first heal and then to help in the reconstruction of the earth.  What a paradox. We need  our dark  side  to create wholeness.  * Vav means  connection or  hook. A connection  can  be good  or bad. We can  be  connected to  Hashem or we can be  hooked  on  almost anything.  This can be a  relationship, a drug, and a way of  thinking. A shadow aspect  of Vav  is this  addiction  or  hook  to those  things that  keep  us  from  our  connection  to  Hashem.  29

*   When you observe an unhealthy connection between people, such as one  following the other’s path, you may have the experience that the two people  are not individuated. This over identification is another shadow aspect of  Vav.  Right Actions for Vav: Because Vav links with words to make connections, you need to use words to  reconnect your heart with those you  love.  *   Have conversations you have avoided with those close to you. Now is a good  time for repair.  *   Remember a time that you blamed another for your own results. Find that person and discuss this with them. Let them know that you are aware of  what you did.  *   Look at an incident or a relationship you have not wanted to resolve or  complete. Take an action in this situation. Allow your heart to speak.  Vulnerability is pure  strength.  * Since  we  only  experience feeling  lost when  we have  disconnected  from Hashem, offer your hand to create a connection with someone in need, someone who might feel lost. Also, accept support from another when you  feel lost or need help. Allow Vav to assist you in this right action.  There is  a  teaching from  Rabbi  Michele from the city of  Zelitchov, a  disciple of the Baal Shem  Tov. He said when you listen to  someone’s  prayers  and  hear what they  ask for; many  times you  hear  cries  for more  and  more  money. In fact,  it is  often difficult to hear  anything else.  However, when you squeeze out the inner  intentions of those sincere  prayers,  you get  Mitzvot  which  mean commandments.  In other words, the  sincere and  true desire of the soul for material  wealth is to  be able to  do  more  good  in  the world  and follow Hashem’s  commandments.  Zayin Meaning:   Sword, woman of valor  30

Focus:   Activity and rest, balance and sustainability  Number:   7  Calendar Connection: Sivan -- May-June When you choose Zayin, it means you are capable of accepting paradox as  your  way of life. The  contradictions life tends  to bring to our  attention  are now  within your understanding. You are being asked to assess your current life situation  with a saber-like precision.  You can expect to experience opposing perspectives in  yourself and in the world while maintaining balance. These perspectives co-exist as  different aspects of reality. You have the choice to see these opposites as a challenge  and a   gift of grace or as a burden and a problem. What  contradictions are  present in your thinking at this time? How do these contradictions affect your spiritual journey?  Zayin  means  sword or weapon. Its spiritual meaning  is a “woman of  valor”, a  bride, and a weapon  of  Spirit who brings  elevated  consciousness and sustenance  to  her marriage. This marriage  is  the  merging of the male  and female  consciousness  within us. The Kabbalah  teaches  that each of us has  this  “woman of  valor” within  whether we are male  or  female. The Baal  Shem Tov taught that Zayin  refers to  woman  because of a verse in proverbs that  reads, "A woman of  valor is  the crown  of  her husband."  The letter Zayin  represents  this  concept in its shape and  form. This feminine  aspect of Zayin has  the power to reveal to the  masculine sword-like aspect of  Zayin,  an innate experience  of  tranquility and resolve.  According to  the Kabbalah, this  same experience  always occurs  during  the Sabbath, the 7 day  of the Kabbalistic week.  These  two meanings represent  the  co-existence  of  paradox in  Zayin.  Do you have a connection  with your  internal  “Woman of  Valor?”  Do you  have  difficulty holding  this  paradox  of  androgyny?  Zayin  also stands for  Zikaron  or memory.  According to the Kabbalah, while  we  are  in  the  womb,  we  learn and integrate  all  the secrets  of the  universe. At our  moment of birth, an angel  pinches our upper lip between our nose and mouth,  and  thus  we  forget  what we  have learned while  preparing  for birth.  It  then becomes our life work to remember  the truth  we  knew  before  we were born. The word  time  (zman)  in  Hebrew  begins  with  Zayin;  as  does  the  word  remember  (zachor) and  remembrance  (zikaron.). The  memory  of  that time  before  we were  born  is the basis  for our  self-identity  and  our purpose  in  Hashem’s creation.  We  have  that memory  within  us and if we  choose  to,  we  can  access  it.  31

Do you remember what you chose for your life work?  The numerical value of Zayan is 7.  *   Shabbat is the seventh day of the week  ¢   There are 7 days of the week *   Seven is considered a beloved number  The Kabbalah teaches that Hashem created the universe in 6 days and rested on  the 7th,   Like Hashem we rest on the seventh day of each week. This is a gift from Hashem not to be refused. It is   a day to remember our purpose here on earth.   We receive an extra measure of our soul on this day of rest. This is the part of our soul that remains dormant all week while we attend to life’s tasks. While we are active, it is difficult to experience this aspect of our soul. During Shabbat, or this seventh day of rest, you meet yourself and this extra measure of your soul is with you.  What does it mean to fully rest?  According to the Kabbalah, humans struggle with life’s challenges in the sword-like, masculine, physical world all week long. Hashem gives you this seventh day to receive the feminine and contemplate His gift of peace and reflection. This is  atime to pray, to sing, to walk, and to play in nature. By creating sacred time on this  seventh day, you are able to bring the energy of the Sabbath to the rest of your week. You can marry the masculine energy of the workweek with the feminine energy of the Sabbath. Remember, Zayin is the sign of a sword, a weapon, anda  symbol of the peace of Shabbat, the bride of the Sabbath. This represents the  paradox of Zayin.  How do you  enjoy the  feminine  aspect of your soul  and  the masculine  aspect of the  physical world?  When you allow yourself to enjoy the pursuit of spiritual endeavors, you experience your longing for greater depth in life. You can then bring this  consciousness and knowledge to the physical plane. You are a spiritual warrior filled  with the freedom of the revelations received on Shabbat.  Shadow  Aspects  of  Zayin:  °   The Sabbath is a day of rest in many religions. However,   over indulging in  rest, food, material wealth, and all other luxuries of life is a shadow aspect of Zayin. It is easy to become spiritually lazy and forget why you are here.  ¢   Inappropriate aggression and maintaining a war-like consciousness is  another shadow aspect of Zayin. The opposite of a spiritual warrior is a  32

power hungry fighter, one who sees and seizes negativity everywhere. This leads to perverting the transformative powers of Zayin - to control others  and experience fear in the world.  ¢   Keeping busy without allowing unstructured space and rest is also a shadow  aspect of Zayin.   The busyness of life without an appreciation of the beingness of life eliminates the potentials inherent in Zayin and leads to  becoming spiritually bereft and desolate. This overwork mentality without  the time to reflect keeps Hashem from permeating your consciousness.  Right Actions for Zayin  Zayin is regarded as the generating and ruling principle over universal  movement. In this movement you learn to control life’s opposites by function of  your will.  ¢   During Shabbat, rest and meditate while acknowledging you may have the  desire to solve a problem, or be busy. *   After Shabbat, bring Hashem into the rest of your week as a partner. Sustain the connection and bring balance to your workweek. *   Do what is right in an important situation. Decide if it is time to act or to wait.  This is the action that will test your partnership with Hashem.  *   Pray or meditate on your Sabbath day. What you experience during that time is especially for you. If an inspiration for action comes, take that action after  Shabbat.  *   Spend time with your family and friends without an agenda. * Use incisiveness, clarity  of mind and intention to safeguard what is  precious  to you. In the Hebrew  Bible, we  read  that when Pharaoh’s  daughter  came to bathe in the Nile  she  spotted a  basket holding a baby.  When  she  realized it was  a  Hebrew  baby,  she knew she had to  make a  quick decision.  Should she  obey  her   father’s decree  that  all Hebrew  babies should be  drowned,  or  should  she  defy  her   father  and everything  he taught  her so  she  could  save  the baby?  The  Bible  states  in  Hebrew,  that  she “sent her  hand maidens to save the baby.” These words can also mean she  personally stretched her arm  out to  reach the basket. The sages  tell us  that even  though  her arm was unable  to  reach  that far through  natural  33

means, a miracle occurred and her hand was able to extend beyond its  natural capacity.  CHET  MEANING:   Life and Fear  FOCUS:   Gateway  to infinity  NUMBER: 8  CALENDAR CONNECTION: Tamuz - June/July  When you choose Chet, it means you are ready to let go of self-limiting  perceptions and open yourself to a more expansive life. Because Chet means both life and fear, these perceptions can be both positive and negative. Many of our life experiences are multifaceted. They are life giving, passionate, and fearful all at the  same time. Falling in love, climbing a Peruvian mountain, and committing to a  spiritual life are just some examples that fit these criteria. What in your experience is both life giving and fearful?  The Kabbalah teaches that when you see yourself and this world without  your ego filters or self-limiting perceptions, you experience awe. This can be fearful.  Three things can happen; you become aware of the preciousness of life, you accept the infinite our life represents, and you confront your fear with wisdom and respect.  When are you in awe of life? The shape of the letter  Chet  combines  both  masculine and feminine  Hebrew letters.  When  connected,  the  energies and  form of these  letters create Chet. This  connection resembles a roof, a bridge,  or even a bridal  canopy  called a Chuppa. This  canopy  connecting masculine and feminine energies stands for  Hashem or  the  infinite.  By choosing  this  letter, you are  ready to include Hashem  as  the third  presence, the connecting force  in your  relationships.  The Kabbalah  teaches  that we have within us a potential  balance of  masculine  and  feminine  energy. Our  choice of an intimate partner  is  influenced  by  what we  lack in  either  of these energies. Our  attraction  to a partner  is based on what  we believe we are  missing,  whether we  are conscious  of  it or not. However,   after  initial attraction  lessens and  we  are  no  longer  seeing through  rose-colored  glasses,  our  perceptions shift  and we tend to  judge  what  we were  once enamored  by. It  is  only when we  let go of  our  judgments  that we accept  Hashem into our  relationships.  Sages  have  said  that  to  initiate  a  relationship  between a  man and  a woman  is  relatively  easy, but  to  maintain  it  is  miraculous, even for  Hashem.  34

What relationships in your life are calling out for this masculine-feminine balance?  How can including Hashem in your relationships support you?  Choosing Chet at this time helps you to have the courage to peel and uncover the veils and skins of this world to receive Hashem in a deeper  more  intimate way. This experience can be an emotional time in your journey. It can bring forth many  past fears and tears. With Chet, you need to walk along this emotional and spiritual  edge of life and fear. Chet calls us to walk this way with compassion  What spiritual edge awaits you? What does this mean to you?  The Kabbalah teaches that Chet transcends nature by bringing life to the dead. This means it is possible to resurrect the dreams and ideals you have given up  for dead. Many tend to forget their dreams as they choose a more practical solution  to their life questions.  Yet, their dreams do not really die. They are  just waiting for  the opportunity to be brought to life again  in a new  way.  With Hashem  as your  partner, it  is now your time to resurrect  your dreams.  The number for Chet is eight.  * The sign for infinity is  a sideways “8”.  ¢ There are eight  days of Chanukah, Passover, and Sukkot  What does it mean for you to choose   a letter that symbolizes the gateway to Infinity,  a letter that goes beyond  nature?  The  Kabbalah  says that  during  Chanukah, it is  possible to go beyond nature  and experience a miracle.  A  miracle can  best  be described as  a victory against  overwhelming odds. This is what happened to  create the  holiday  of Chanukah. There  was a military  victory that  went against  all odds, and  the  oil  that  should  have  lasted  one day stayed lit for eight.  Chet  brings  the  lights  of chaos  into  the vessels  of  order.  This means take a  risk.  This means  experience  the  unknown,  while  staying  connected to  Hashem. The  Kabbalah teaches  that  the energy of the Chet  has  to  do with Hashem  “hovering”  over  the  world. When  Hashem  hovers over his  created  world, He is  continuing  to  sustain and  nourish  His  world  while  at  the same  time  allowing  all the creatures in this  world  to live  independently.  When you  choose Chet,  you  are  about to do  the  same.  You  have chosen to  defy  the  gravity of your  personal  world  and leap  into the  chaos  35

of spiritual joy. This is not an easy task. Although you may feel afraid at times, you  are ready.  Shadow Aspects of Chet:  ¢   Walking through the emotional and spiritual edge of life and fear can create a form of paralysis or behavior that is thoughtless or dangerous. Both of these extremes are equal in their creation of repetitive negativity. This shadow aspect of Chet can be insidious and challenging  unless  fears  are made an ally.  *   Staying in our comfort zone and acting out of a spiritually costumed self-  interest is another shadow aspect of Chet. Many people pretend they are living life fully and have accepted fear as a friend and ally, while in reality  they have not.  ¢   Chet’s shadow blames Hashem when life is difficult. This shadow aspect of Chet also denies the possibility to accept personal responsibility for mistakes.  Right Actions for Chet:  ©   Look for places in your life where you are resting in your comfort zones. Pick one to explore. Take an action that has an “awesome” risk to it.  ° The next  time  you  make a mistake, tell  eight people, the  number  for Chet  without making excuses or blaming anyone, including yourself.  ¢ Share from your heart and allow yourself to feel the  fear intimacy demands.  As you make this fear your ally, you will allow more intimacy into your  relationships.  Reb Shlomo Carlebach,  asked, “ Do you know  how  the  BAL Sham  Tov  defined  Heaven  and Hell  “ He then  continued,” After  a thousand  years all of us  go  up  to  heaven for the  heavenly court.  There they show  us  36

two movies. One movie depicts how we  were in life  and the other what we  could  have been. If the two movies match, that is heaven.  But, if they are  not alike, that is hell.”  Tet  Meaning: Womb and  Serpent  Focus: Concealed good  Number:   9  Calendar Connection:   Month of Av  When  you choose Tet,  it means you are  in the state of “becoming”  true to  yourself. Hashem has  held you closely,  in a place of “goodness” and  the incubation  stage  is  complete. You can now emerge from the womb of becoming, to  the world  of  being, to shed that which no longer  serves your goals  and desires.  What aspect of your  history does  not  serve you  now?  How has your goodness  been incubating?  Tet is the first letter  of the word beauty in  the Hebrew language  and  also  one  of the eight  synonyms  for the word beauty. Tet also  is  the first  letter of the word  Tov, meaning “good.” Tet refers to  the level  of beauty bathed  in modesty  --the  ability  of  beauty to  be partially concealed  and introverted during  its  gestation  period.  How does your beauty  and  modesty  show up  in  the world? However, by choosing Hashem and  learning about myself, I was able to transform those despicable traits into  a  person refined enough  to be able to encounter  and reflect the face of  Hashem.  Reish  Meaning:   Wicked, poor, evil, head or beginning, inherit  Number:   200  Focus:   Clarifying choices  Calendar  Connection: Friday - 6" day  of the week  When  you  choose Reish, it means you  have  the capability to transform  negativity  and “amorality” into  healing  and goodness.  It also  means  you  can now  make way for  new beginnings. Reish is a letter of extreme  transformative  possibilities both  negative  and positive. Although it is  located  near  the end of the  Alef-Bet, Reish means  beginning.  What  new beginnings  have you  experienced?  Are  there  negative  situations  you wish to transform? The  Kabbalah  teaches that wisdom begins with the  fear of Hashem. This  Kabbalistic concept  of fear is not familiar to  us. Imagine  this fear  as alive,  similar to a lightning bolt. This bolt  of fear shocks the ego. It  then  turns  into  awe, which breaks through the  patterns  keeping us from  having  new  “beginnings”. These  new  “beginnings” are  paradigm shifts  that  allow us to  experience  the  wisdom of Hashem.  Are there  recent  experiences that allowed  you  to have  an “aha”  of  this nature?  The  Kabbalah  teaches that  we  are born  knowing  “selflessness.”  Selflessness is  an inner experience  of the soul and  serves as a container to  hold  new  flashes  of  insight  and  wisdom.  Fear,   the beginning  of wisdom,  corresponds to  the source  of  this state  of  selflessness.  Fear "shocks" ego, dissolving  the hardness  of the  heart that  prevents  us  from  perceiving  outside  of  our  own reality. This  “shock” allows us  to  see  outside  of  our limited  perspective  and  assists  us in  recognizing  the  Divine in  all  creation.  72

Have you  experienced  “ego shock?”  What was the result?  By definition,  Reish also  means “wicked”, “evil”, “poor”, and  “head”.   Fear can  be disguised as resistance to the light. By fearing Hashem, and removing this  disguise, it is possible to return to him through acts of repentance. These words and concepts may seem harsh and  outdated  in today’s world  of spoken light and  easy  spirituality. Yet, fear of the light is omnipresent  in  our lives.  It can shatter  our  pictures of ourselves. It can stop us  from accepting love from  our friends and family.  It  defines our  external world.  By  allowing  love and rejecting the “poverty  of our  soul,”  we can reclaim our  “selflessness.” This reclamation  then  gives us the power to  transform our negativity  into  compassion and  acceptance.  What are the ways  that  you are  “selfless?”  Our minds  create  context for all situations. The basis of all human creation  begins with an interpretation of experience. This interpretation becomes  the context  for the story of our life. We then choose behaviors from  our interpretation that  continue to support  what is often  referred to as “our  story.” This “story” becomes  our reality. When we allow fear of Hashem  to shock  our ego, we can consistently  enjoy  new beginnings and let go of our  story.  Rosh Hashanah is  the Jewish New Year and  begins with the letter Reish. This  holiday is  about new beginnings. It is  the time of the year  when anyone can return  to Hashem. Although  this can  happen  at any  time, the energy  that  surrounds Rosh  Hashanah precipitates  this  return.  When  we completely atone  for our mistakes, we become a “Rosh,” a leader  for our own  growth. In  fact, one of the  prayers  during the  Rosh  Hashanah meal is to act as the  “head” and not as the “tail” in  the  coming year. This means leading  in  righteous actions and not following  others  in  poor behavior.  Rosh  Hashanah is  the Kabbalistic celebration  of the birthday of the  world.  What celebrations do you  observe  that  lead you  to  take “right”  actions?  Hashem’s  desire for  the world had a context,  a  head. This context  is  the  physical, intellectual, emotional  and spiritual environment of the  world.  Breishit, a  word in the  beginning of Genesis,  shows us that  we  create our  lives  in  context  at  all  times.  How we  interpret  our  life  situation determines our experience.  The same  situation,  given a different context  presents a myriad of  possibilities.  This is  the  beauty  of all  creation.  What  appears to  be  a piece  of  marble  becomes  the statue of  David  to the artist  Michelangelo.  The  number  for Reish  is 200.  73

Shadow side of Reish  When we deny what is going on in our lives and pretend to have no fear of Hashem, we resist being in the light. This denial eventually snowballs into a solid structure that can only be melted with fear of Hashem.   Remember, fear  is awe.  Worshiping our attachments by defending and protecting them from   is another shadow aspect of Reish. Attachments to material, spiritual, physical  or emotional energy and objects lead to a lack of wisdom and selfishness. The context of this life-style is hardening of heart and mind. This hardening creates brittle thinking and un-experienced feelings. Negativity and hurtful  behavior is the result.  Sin is knowingly choosing actions that will hurt the soul. The concept of sin,  although seemingly antiquated, is still present in the collective consciousness  ofthe   mind. This is   a shadow aspect of Reish. Although sin is in the heart and mind of the “sinner,”   the effect of negative behavior on the environment  and the people in that environment is palpable.  Right action for Reish  Recognize your true  emptiness.  Identify an attachment  and choose to  let  it  go. Notice your  reaction to this choice. Take the actions needed to make  this  change. Allow your  natural goodness to reassert  itself. Choose to take an action based  solely on your goodness.  Pray or  meditate with the love of Hashem in your heart  and mind. Go deep  into your  experience and embrace any  thoughts and feelings that arise.  You  may receive a glimpse of  infinity.  This can  occur  at  any  time.  14

A Rabbi  was  sitting  with  his  disciples eating  the “third meal,” at  what  was  considered  the holiest  moment of the week, the  Sabbath day  right before  sunset.  The Rabbi  was teaching a  mystical  discourse  about the four worlds of creation,  the  highest of which  is  called  “Olam Atzilut,” the world of emanation.   The disciples were  concentrating  with  intense   focus. Suddenly  the Rabbi  began to  cough  persistently. His  young  son  brought  him some water to  drink,  but the Rabbi  waved  him  away,  saying,  “In the  world of Atzilut no  one  needs  to drink  water.” The  715

young boy replied politely butfirmly, “Tatte (daddy) in the world of  Atzilut no one coughs either.”  Shin  Meaning:   Fire, tooth, change, year, sleep, teach, two, sharp,  Number: 300  Focus:   Finding changeless essence  Calendar Connection:   Summer When you choose Shin, it means you have an unfaltering awareness of the natural rhythms of the seasons and of the human need for wholeness. In order for this  wholeness to occur, you are prepared to overcome  the  challenge  of dualistic thinking.  You  know that although our  planet  is moving toward  wholeness and harmony, at the same time we are seriously engaged in wars, bigotry, genocide,  political deviousness and  more. We have  the  choice to look  at this as  good  and evil,  right  and wrong  or simply as  degrees of totality.  What “right and wrong” thinking is most difficult for you to digest?  Shin has more meanings  than any other  Hebrew letter.  A central  meaning of Shin  is  change. You  are  aware  that change  is  part of the  natural  rhythm of life. What  doesn’t change  is reality; and reality is  Hashem. The Kabbalah  teaches that  when Hashem  created  the world, he put before us a challenge  --- to find “changeless  essence”  in  the physical  world.  This changeless  essence is  Him. Change  is  the illusion.  Yet, to live in  the  physical  world,  we  live as if change  is  the reality and at  times  as if Hashem  is  the illusion. Eastern  philosophies  stress  these teachings as well.   .  What personal  experiences  have led to know Hashem is reality?  Paradoxically,  the  letter  Shin  is used in Kabbalistic  meditation as a symbol of Divine, never  changing,  light. In this  meditation, Shin  is  commonly  associated  with  the  element  of  fire.  It  is  imagined  hovering  above the  head of the  person meditating  as  shooting  flames.  When  we think of a flame  we  can  see its two  aspects.  The inner  part  of the  flame  stays  constant, while the  outer  flame is continuously  in a state of movement.  The  Kabbalah says,  “In  the  world  to come,  the changeless  essence will  reveal  itself  within  the flame.”  When you  meditate,  what  do  you  focus on? Is it  your  breath,  an image, a sound,  etc.?  76

Another meaning of Shin is tooth or fang. When  we  chew on anything,  we  decompose  it;  yet, the  essence of what we chew does not decompose. Whether  we  chew on food, thoughts, or feelings, we  retain the  essence of that which  we  decompose, whether  by mouth or  mind. This is a prevalent concept in  kosher animal  slaughter.  The Kabbalah  teaches that the  essence of the food and liquid we eat  and  drink stays and becomes part of us. The name of the  person who performs  ritual  slaughter of animals is Shochet. It too,  begins with a Shin.  What do you chew on when you get  into bed at night? What essence  is still  with you  in  the morning  when you awaken?  Another  word  that begins with Shin is Shalom, meaning peace  and  wholeness.   Shalom  is  also a name for Hashem. This Shalom or peace, presents itself  most dominantly on Shabbat, or the Sabbath - another  word  that begins with a Shin.  The Kabbalah teaches  that the  Sabbath  is a taste of the  world to come and allows  humans the opportunity to give up dualistic  thinking for  25 hours  at a time.  Is it possible for you to experience both  peace  and war  at the  same time?  What is  that like?  The  number  for Shin  is 300, the completion  of the  number three.  The  Shadow  Aspect  of Shin:  ¢ Corrupting  spiritual  truths  by  personal  distortion disguised as knowing  or excessive  humility is a shadow  aspect  of Shin. Many  religious  zealots preach  of the fires of hell, when  their  audience does not  believe  their  rhetoric.  If one  looks  closely,  they can  see  the preacher’s own  fire  of hell. As humans,  we  cannot know all there  is to know, and by tricking ourselves  in  that manner, we  distort our  strengths into foolish  absolutes. We then  lose  our ability to  experience the  essence of  reality, Hashem.  * Lack of joy is  another  shadow aspect  of Shin. Without the  cleansing flame ofa  continuous intention  of  self-awareness, and growth,  there cannot be joy.  Joy  is different  than  externally  motivated happiness that  comes  and  goes.  Continuous  lack of  joy  eventually turns that  cleansing  flame  into  ash.  ¢ Greed,  constant distractions, biting words, shallow  connections, rigid  beliefs,  and an unwillingness  to  dive into  the depths  of the  unchanging essence of  Hashem, is yet  another shadow aspect of  Shin.  Without  the  experience of  depth both  with  the self and with  others, the eternal flame  of  Shin cannot be  experienced.  Without this  depth, people  become  robotic,  unable to feel  the  joy and  humility of  life.  77

Right Actions for Shin  ¢   Speak your simple truth in all situations of change and chaos. Notice what  happens to any thoughts of distortion or embellishment not spoken. Be  aware of your desire to say more or less.  ° Meditate on a flame. Notice the interplay between the  unchanging  inner  flame and the changing outer flame.  ¢ Discover the inherent goodness in each interaction  or situation you  take part  in. Allow that goodness to determine your action.  ¢ Seek your  spiritual path with  consistency and vigor. Be aware of other’s  truths’ and find joy in the similarities and differences  Every book of   Biblical  and Rabbinic  commentary  begins  with  the letter  Beit,  the second  letter of the  Alef-Bet.   You will not find a  Hebrew sacred  text  starting with  the  letter Aleph, the first letter of the  Alef-Bet. This  is because  even  when you  think   you  have completed your  learning and have gotten  all the way to the letter Tav, the end of the Hebrew Alef-Bet, you  have  actually not  even  mastered the Aleph,  the  very  beginning.  78

Tav  Focus:  Living in  state of duality knowing  there is  absolute  truth  Meaning: A   sign, a mark  Number: 400  Calendar Connection:   Saturday - 7" day of the week  When  you choose Tay, it means you  are balanced in your quest to align with  universal reality, the reality of Hashem. The only absolute truth is Hashem. Through Tav, we have a taste of that  truth. Hashem is the real  story.  When  we meditate on Tav, we understand that knowledge is  not the end of knowing. In fact, it is  the  beginning of the next  cycle of learning. Though Tav is  the final  letter of the Hebrew  alphabet,  truth is  our  final destination.  What does truth mean to you?  Can you  tell  when another is speaking their  truth?  Tav represents  the  end of one stage of completion in our  life and  the beginning of the next stage. We are always in  a  state of completion.  Becoming complete  or whole  may mean leaving something we  are  attached to. Many  experience that as  a  death. Sometimes it may be so. Becoming  complete with a  particular situation allows us  to  see it for what  it is. . However,   we  still know there is always more  than meets our  eye; we cannot  ever  know Hashem from the limits  of  our  human  mind. If we can describe an experience, it is  not the truth of Hashem.  Hashem is  unknowable. Truth is  the seal of Hashem.  What situations do you need to complete? What  situations,  relationships, etc. have been difficult for  you to complete?  Tav means  seal. Many  Hebrew Holy words begin with the Tav. Tikun Olam  means to “make  whole.”  The  Kabbalah  teaches  that  in order for creation to occur, matter  was embedded with  shards  of  holiness and  light.  It becomes  the task  of humans  to liberate those  shards  of  holiness, elevate  them, and  return  them to  Hashem. Until  that occurs,  we  are trapped in our minds  and  cannot  see a larger  truth. Are  you overlooking  the  existence  of  holiness in  your life? Where?  What  larger truth  do  you connect into  to feel  complete?  719

Another word that begins with Tav is “tefila” which means prayer. The Kabbalah instructs us to pray and meditate with heart and devotion so that our intention will reach Hashem.   Because Tav is a symbol reflecting the center of our psyches, it is the receptacle of creation for all our human truth. What is your intention when you pray?   Do you ask for something from Hashem?  Are you giving thanks? The number for Tav is 400  Shadow Aspect of Tav  Being in an overconfident and arrogant state is a shadow aspect of Tav. Many people who are in this state see themselves as “perfect” not needing to change anything about themselves. This way of being can be devastating to  our perfect person, as others see what they are blind to.   Instead, the perfect person tries to change others so they themselves do not have to change. Over  time, they become incapable of change.  Thinking all is complete when in fact, there is quite a bit of disarray in one’s life is  also a shadow aspect of Tav. It  is a form of denial.  Staying in a situation when truths are  not being shared  can damage  them  permanently. This is a total  avoidance of intimacy. Marriages fail, children  leave home  angry and hurt, and businesses fail  when a person is unaware of  other’s feelings,  thoughts,  and dreams.  Putting  one’s  “seal” on a lie is  the  same as saying no  to Hashem. This too, is a shadow aspect of Tav.  Right  Actions for Tav  Be  humble  in  the  face of Hashem. Allow  yourself to  meditate, pray and  spend  time  each  day  with Hashem. Write  down your thoughts  or  share  them with a  friend.  When asked a question,  tell  your  truth  with nothing  added or  withheld.  The  power of  your  truth lies  in  its results.  As  you do  this   watch your  level of  intimacy  increase  and your  self-confidence grow. Complete relationships that are keeping you from being in  present time  with  others  in  your  life.  This  means  taking care of leftover  thoughts and  actions.  80

Authors Notes  Judith  Orloff,  M.Ed.  When  I  was a small child, I lost a  mitten  and was  inconsolable. My mom offered hugs,  new  mittens,  ice  cream  and  lots of  love.  When  able  to  speak, I said the  lost  mitten  would be lonely for  its  mate.  I thought  it  was alive and had feelings.  I later discovered  in my  work that  many  children feel  that  way about  lost toys  or clothes.   When  I  read fairy  tales,  1 often felt bad for the wicked stepsisters  and  the wicked queens  or  witches  in the  stories. I couldn’t understand why  they  were  so  mean. | also  didn’t understand  why the  heroes  81

and heroines of these stories were always so good. These are just two examples of how I  thought as a child.  Working with Lubavitch of Bucks County, co-designing programs about G-d, holiness and the practical application of the Kabbalah, my love of writing, and meeting Yehudis  Fishman and Jasmyne Boswell, led me to write a book about the Power of the Sacred Living Letters, the Hebrew Alef- Bet.  I had many Ab-has’ while working with Lubavitch of Bucks County. I realized all of  Hashem’s creation has a soul, and there is a shadow aspect of all living creatures. I also  learned that we each have a moment-to-moment opportunity to tip the scales into goodness  through  right actions.  Jasmyne and   I realized although we both followed spiritual paths most of our lives, and were Jewish by birth, neither one of us knew much about the mystical aspect of Judaism. Ihad only recently been learning how to read Hebrew and wanted to study the meaning  of the letters. Together with Jasmyne and Yehudis, I have been on a journey into the core of Judaism, the Sacred Living Letters, and this is only a beginning. What a joy to  discover Judaism has a mystical aspect that is unending and infinite.  Writing this  book led  me  to many  personal  and transpersonal discoveries. I know I am a  spark of  G-d, of Hashem. This discovery obligates me  to do right actions, and embrace shadow  aspects of myself rather  than project them onto  others. To  recognize that Styrofoam,  plastic, and all that is here  has G-d in it, has shifted how I live  my life.  I am a spiritual guide,  coach,  non-dual, transpersonal  therapist  and author.  I know we  are all connected  through the always present, no-thingness of Hashem. I cherish  my time  with  clients and  feel  privileged and honored  to  accompany them on their  journey.  I  wish  you  blessings and love  in your personal exploration of  The Sacred Living Letters.  JASMYNE BOSWELL  Writing The  Power  of the Sacred Letters  opened my heart  and mind  to a deeper  perspective  of life and its preciousness.  Although  I was  brought  up in a Reform  Jewish household,  my parents never  belonged  to a temple or synagogue. We did celebrate  Passover, and  were  allowed to  stay home  from  school  on High  Holidays, but  my  knowledge of Judaism  was  very limited.  I became  interested in spirituality in my  late  20’s, studying various forms of  Psychology,  Hinduism, and Buddhism, never  knowing  that my own religion  had deep mystical  and  spiritual  roots.  82

It wasn’t until I heard talk about the Kabbalah in my early 50’s and started reading and  going to lectures that my interest peaked. I was excited to learn that my religious heritage was steeped in wisdom, dating back to the beginning of time.   My discovery of these  ancient teachings opened a door to my great appreciation of Judaism.  My inspiration for writing The Power of the Sacred Letters came from my personal interest in learning about the Kabbalah. I loved losing myself in the myriad of writings on the subject. I wanted a deep, personal experience of its wisdom and didn’t have the time  to invest in reading all the formal texts.  For years I used  the Celtic Runes,  Oracles  known by most spiritual seekers, on a semi-  regular basis. I enjoyed the immediacy of the teachings that gave me the momentary  guidance I was seeking. However,   after time, [ knew what the rune I picked would say before even  reading the text. One  morning, a thought  came to me while I was  meditating—a Kabbalistic version of the Runes. Because  we  enjoyed and respected each other’s  life experiences and  perspectives,  we knew we  could learn from one another. We would bring our  complimentary  gifts together  in the spirit of Kabbalah. Judith Orloff Critique of a Dissertation: Nowhere Man  Skipp, Tracy John Educational Leadership (2010) ELC 727 Methods Action Research Dr. Anna DiStefano  3/11/17  Complete description of the study including the author’s line of reasoning Reading this dissertation was a complete surprise.   I chose an Action  Research Dissertation that used   the autoethnography methodology.  In this dissertation,   Nowhere Man: Autoethnographic Reflections on Identity,  Family, and Leadership, Skipp describes the purpose of his self-study to  “discover the values and attitudes I model as a leader to support people in  doing their best work. Specifically, do I practice leadership Intimacy?”p.viii. One of his goals in this dissertation is to bring the reader into his experience so they  can be with him on this journey.   In that goal, he succeeded.   As I read, I felt as  absorbed as when I read a good novel.   Chapter One, Context for the Study, begins with a quote from John Lennon and Paul McCartney, which represents  why he chose the title Nowhere Man for this work.   “Knows not where he’s going to; isn’t he a   bit like you and me?” Skipp begins by describing his life through his memories, thoughts, and feelings.   After a discussion on the history of the University, he describes his upbringing. Being a “military brat," he found solace through his Catholic schooling in the countries where his father was stationed.   His writing is deeply  personal and arises from one of his five methods of research, Autoethnography  as well as a strong desire to heal himself. The other methods are a 360 assessment, Interviews, Reflective  Journaling and Peer Debriefing.   He chose authethnography for this exploration

through his values of Franciscan Roman Catholicism and his life as a senior  administrator in a traditional university. To him, those values were in constant  conflict.   I believed he needed to resolve his daily struggle between “who I see myself to be, and who other students, faculty, and staff perceive me to be  (Jourard,  1971)  He suffered every day of his life with pain from rheumatoid arthritis. In the first year of his Doctoral work,   his wife who he had been with since he was 15, asked him to “let me go,”   I view his choice of using autoethnography, as well as a 360 assessment which included his children, and interviews with his  supervisor and peers as   a   brilliant resolve to his mounting life crises. And, he certainly achieved the purpose of bringing the reader, me,   into his everyday life as   I was and am moved to tears, heartbreak, and tenderness as  he unswervingly struggles to achieve his goal of “leadership intimacy." (p.68)  He describes leadership intimacy as authenticity, and authenticity as  knowing oneself.   He continually identifies with   Saint Francis of Assisi, a  Catholic saint, medieval monk, and mystic, who also struggled with the question of “who am I” daily.” His deep respect for the values of the Franciscans and his ideas of what a university should be like   provides a  reflection of his ontology and epistemology. One of his research questions is “who is training the future generation of leaders?   He makes the case that the   University is no longer a facility where formal leadership occurs.   He believes that leadership intimacy may be a way to offer the leadership mentoring and modeling that he believes is not available  presently in universities based on the new economic reality of funding, etc.  Operating on a   fixed seniority system with a pool of only the most senior staff [faculty] is a very different atmosphere than the corporate fast track model for  young executives with obvious, demonstrated talent (Hearn, 2003).  He uses three key concepts to frame his study:  e   The philosophy of personalism

e The  practice  of intimacy  e   The role of fatherhood   within a family context  Throughout this study,   his cognitive dissonance about who he is evident.  He works every day as a middle-level administrator in a traditional University and his desire to share the theory of   “leadership intimacy, ” from his personal  conflicts. He moves between Marxist and Roman Catholic values in much of his study. The ‘Idea of a University’ was   a   village with its priests.”   Whereas, “the ‘Idea of a Modern University’ was a town - a one-industry town - with its intellectual oligarchy.” (Kerr, 2001p.3)   And then he says, “The complex multiversities” have seamlessly morphed into transnational corporations, born of necessity.”   His choice of becoming a Personalist brings his internal war between his Roman Catholic values and the big business attitude of universities to a halt.  . Personalists maintain that a person, being partly spiritual, is not wholly governed by the laws of physics; and within certain limits, can exercise free will  and as such are not completely predictable.  . Personalists accept axiology, or value-theory and disagree with the logical  positivists (influenced by science) affirming the absolute value of each person.  (Gregg, 1999, pp. 167-168)  His belief of how to be a   leader, father, ex-husband, and administrator are reflected in the following quote:   "It is through our responses to other persons that we become persons. It is others who challenge, enlighten and enrich us. There is no such thing as an isolated individual Reality is the lived  relation. Through sharing in the giving and receiving of mutual being the, "I"  becomes real.” (Oldham, 1958)  Literature Search and Review His Literature Review was motivated by   a   crisis as to whether he was

sufficiently prepared (p. 27) to lead.   I find throughout the dissertation, a  continuing attempt to prove he is o.k. as a person.   He shares many stories  about the people he works.   The most poignant is a confrontation he has with  his supervisor where she tells him because he is not a faculty member, he is like the water boy on the team. "she was also prone to fits of rage." (p.28)  With a dearth of literature on Intimacy Leadership. He explored,  e Visionary Leadership  e   Collaborative Leadership e   Reflective Leadership  e   Communicative Leadership  e   Relational Leadership  After a thorough review of these leadership methodologies, he said,  “none of them frame my professional experience or leadership practice (Raelin, 2003). Perhaps this is because traditional leadership is   often studied in a business model.”   Rather, he approached his most coveted mentor, Brother Richard, a Franciscan monk that lived a few blocks away and tended the garden  in the church, and spoke   to him of what he learned in his literature search,  “I guess I would see leadership in three parts,” I explained. “The first part is intimacy with self; you must disclose self to authentically know yourself, and you must know yourself to get to know others. The second part is intimacy with others, from a personalist perspective or philosophy, it relies on relationships to exist. The third part is developmental intimacy; you must give others a safe place to grow and nurture those relationships. We need those relationships to exist. It is a circular flow, a process that we continually go through life.”(p.48)  Research Methods

Reflexive poetics:   This comes from two similar strategies, reflexive ethnography (Ellis & Bochner, 1996) and anthropological poetics (Brady 1991. Uses internal dialogue, conversations with self to evoke strong feelings in the reader. Visual form of evocative narrative (Bochner & Ellis 1997) Autoethnography: the Personal style of writing known as narrative inquiry, (Bochner, Ellis, Tillman-Healy, 1997, 1998)   "A stream of consciousness  like watching a film.   An intensely personal format for social science that  invites the reader into the mind and thoughts of the researcher." Research Questions The purpose of this study is to investigate the following assumptions and questions: ©   Does being insightful in personal day to day activities andin   relationships lead toa  deeper level of mindfulness?  ¢   Does experiencing insight lead to behavior benefiting the participant and the people they  interact with on a regular basis? ©   Does experiencing insight reduce blame as a function of projection. Projection as a resistance to insight is a habit everyone learns as a child. It is so ingrained that most of us think it is a natural part of who we are. However, it is not intrinsic to our nature, but learned. It happens when people do not approve of   their feelings and fool themselves into believing the feelings are coming from someone else. When we project, we see ourselves as victims of someone else’s actions rather than being the author of our own experience. To be truly self-aware it is necessary to see ourselves as being responsible for our own experience (Malin& Grotstein 1966;) (Orloff & Doubleday 1991)

MINDFULNESS AND INSIGHT ACTION RESEARCH   PROJECT   7 Research Approach I will use narrative inquiry, a qualitative action research methodology, for this study. Through narrative inquiry, a participant’s experience is interpreted and made personally meaningful (Clandinin, Pushor, & Orr, 2007, p. 22).   It is a story and a way of thinking about experience (Clandinin et al., 2007, p. 22).   Narrative inquirers turn from one way of knowing the world to an understanding that there are multiple ways of knowing and understanding human experience (Clandinin, 2006, p. 25). I think Narrative Inquiry methodology will allow for a more  historically accurate interview through the in-depth interview itself. The connection between the  researcher, myself, and the participant will bring forth data not otherwise elicited. “Narrative is both a qualitative research method and way of theorizing psychological and social phenomena” (Carless & Douglas, 2017, p. 307). Narrative inquiry is first and foremost a  way of understanding experience. It is also a research methodology. “It is, then, both a view of  the phenomena of people's experiences and a methodology for narratively inquiring into  experience and thus allows for the intimate study of individuals’ experiences over time and in context” (Given, 2008, p. 542). This is important in analyzing the data.  Narrative inquiry needs to be authentic and transparent.   The idea of the researcher’ s voice and the voice of the participant needs to be faithful to the historical and future context of the study. Each participant is telling their story as reflected to the researcher who also has a voice.   “to live authentically, you must follow your own way” (Taylor, 1997). ‘Narratives may provide a fundamental connection for action research. Creswell, 2005 stated, “they emphasize close collaboration with the participant-storyteller” (p.?).

Research Design  The design is based on narrative inquiry, is qualitative and will use surveys, in-depth interviews and focus group exit interviews. Twenty participants will be given an in-depth questionnaire and interview to begin with. This will be followed by an email based daily survey  for 28 days. Both the action and the reflection will be based on the principle of insight.  The next day, the participant will be asked to share the results of their choice and this will be  categorized by an algorithm specifically designed for this study.   Each participant will participate in a focus group exit interview following the 28-day email survey. The actions and reflections the participants are asked to complete are based on previous focus groups and a 1000-person questionnaire previously administered. Plan for Analyzing the Data ‘The narrative inquiry approach used in this study values collaboration and relationships. | Disabilities Sensitivity Training  al  Anti-Bullying Workshop  History  a i   i   i   i   i families  The Friendship Circle, founded in 1994 in Detroit, Michigan, extends a helping hand to  who have chil n and teenagers with special  needs, ranging   from   muscular dystrophy to  autism, and involves   them ina full  range of social, recreational and respite opportunities.  The Friendship Circle also   fills a vital  need for meaningful  volunteer   opportunities t  who,  with the of professional  social workers, provide the respite and friendship to   the  families and children. All  teen  volunteers participate in intensive   training, including onsite  guidance and seminars given  by  professionals in the field.  Through  this unique  formula of shared experiences, all are enriched:  «The child/teen with  special needs  looks forward  to the opportunity to  play with  and  learn  from their friends and appreciates the companionship of peers  which is often times  lacking, in their lives.  « The teenage  volunteer  learns the  value of giving,  and cherishes   the  experience of  making a difference in a  child's life  and  bringing a smile to his or her face.  «The child's   family  receives a needed  respite and the pleasure of seeing their child  become a part of the community.  -the  Friendship Circle programs include home  respite  visits, music,  sports  and  art   therapy  programs, summer  and winter  camps,  and much  more.  The Detroit model has  since  been  replicated in 42  cities across the United States, with  many  others looking to start  the program  in the near  future.  Currently,  more   than 3,000 families  who  have children, with special needs  benefit from our programs. The teen volunteer  club boasts  5,500 members  nationwide  and is  growing. The impact of the Friendship  Circle is multiplied  by  the friendships and  support system that  grows between the families of   the volunteers  and the  special  needs families. Thus by  extension the  Circle  actually  includes tens of thousands of  people. \  Each in lent Friendship Circle is  operated  by  its  local center, and  all  operations and  programs arg supported  entirely  by  the local  community of each  Friendship  Circle. Sensitizing  teenagers  to  the challenges that people with  disabilities face and  making them  aware of the commonalties that unite  us all is  the first step towards providing anioverall respect  for each  person’s  differences,  be they physical,  racial,  socioeconomic or otherwise, and  providing teenagers with the skills  necessary  for looking  beyond differences  to find the  similarities that friendships can be built on. With sensitivity and the  ability  to reach  out to  others,  teenagers  are much less likely  to bully their  peers  as this behavior is  most often the  outgrowth of a lack  of sensitivity  and  a sense that differences are inherently bad and often  times insurmountable. Instead  teenagers  are encouraged to find  common  ground  with each  other  and form friendships.  The positive  effect of disability  sensitivity training  on teenagers and the resulting  decrease in  bullying behavior has  been evidenced  so far in our research. We have found that teens  who  volunteer  with the Friendship Circle and other similar  programs have  also become more  respectful and understanding towards peers  who  are labeled as “outcasts” because of their  differences. In addition, these  volunteers  are much less likely  to engage in bullying activities  when compared to  the overall communal  and  school population. f  The proposed one-day workshop will  include  discussions,  improvisational exercises and videos  directed  by a trained facilitator to help  involve the  teens in the learning  process. | Each  participant will  be asked to  assume  scenarios and  navigate  challenges that  are routinely experienced  by people with disabilities and to engage in discussions  and develo ) ideas for }  surpassing  these situations. The facilitator will  then engage the  teenagers to translate the /  lessons  learned  from  these  experiences to the differences and challenges faced by those within = /  the  teens’ peer  groups  and community.
